title: Two Tesla Model X cars stopped as a 400-year-old oak fell across the A31 at Sturminster Marshall during Storm Dennis; eight occupants walked away, and automatic emergency braking may have saved them
summary: Two Model X cars stopped as an oak fell on the A31 in Storm Dennis; eight occupants walked away, both drivers credit the emergency brakes.
account: On the evening of Saturday 15 February 2020, during Storm Dennis, a 400-year-old oak fell across the A31 at Sturminster Marshall, Dorset. It hit two Tesla Model X cars going in opposite directions. Laurence Sanderson of Brentwood, Essex, was driving wife Anna and three children to a half-term holiday. He told the Mirror the car was on Autopilot, the emergency braking kicked in and the trunk landed on the bonnet. The other car, a Tesla loan vehicle driven by Josh Whitelock of Wimborne with Kitty McConnell and her mother Julia, also stopped suddenly. Whitelock told the Bournemouth Echo he was not sure its automatic brakes were enabled. Anna Sanderson had two black eyes and bruising. Nobody was seriously hurt.
purpose: Tesla's Autopilot hardware and software provide driver assistance and active safety features including Automatic Emergency Braking. It detects obstacles the car may hit and applies the brakes. Stopping short of a falling tree is that intended use as the drivers describe it.
system: Tesla Autopilot driver-assistance suite with Automatic Emergency Braking, on two Model X cars
model_version: Not reported; both cars were Tesla Model X, one a Tesla loan car, and no Autopilot hardware or software version is given

ratings.reason: A 400-year-old oak struck two cars at the bonnet. Eight people walked away with, at worst, two black eyes, a bump on the head and bruising. Both drivers and the Mirror call it life-saving. But that rests on the drivers' accounts, no telemetry or official assessment is reported, and the second driver was unsure the brakes were enabled.

ai_role.statement: By Laurence Sanderson's account his car was on Autopilot and the emergency braking stopped it so the trunk hit the bonnet rather than the cabin. Josh Whitelock said he was not sure whether his loan car's automatic brakes were enabled and credited its other safety features. No Tesla data, police finding or engineering assessment of whether either system braked, or whether the drivers would have stopped in time themselves, is reported. Elon Musk's reply, “Glad you're all ok”, acknowledges the outcome, not the mechanism.

fields.account: On the evening of Saturday 15 February 2020, during Storm Dennis, a 400-year-old oak fell across the A31 at Sturminster Marshall, Dorset. It hit two Tesla Model X cars going in opposite directions. Laurence Sanderson of Brentwood, Essex, was driving wife Anna and three children to a half-term holiday. He told the Mirror the car was on Autopilot, the emergency braking kicked in and the trunk landed on the bonnet. The other car, a Tesla loan vehicle driven by Josh Whitelock of Wimborne with Kitty McConnell and her mother Julia, also stopped suddenly. Whitelock told the Bournemouth Echo he was not sure its automatic brakes were enabled. Anna Sanderson had two black eyes and bruising. Nobody was seriously hurt.

fields.account: On the evening of Saturday 15 February 2020, during Storm Dennis, a 400-year-old oak fell across the A31 at Sturminster Marshall, Dorset. It hit two Tesla Model X cars going in opposite directions. Laurence Sanderson of Brentwood, Essex, was driving wife Anna and three children to a half-term holiday. He told the Mirror the car was on Autopilot, the emergency braking kicked in and the trunk landed on the bonnet. The other car, a Tesla loan vehicle driven by Josh Whitelock of Wimborne with Kitty McConnell and her mother Julia, also stopped suddenly. Whitelock told the Bournemouth Echo he was not sure its automatic brakes were enabled. Anna Sanderson had two black eyes and bruising. Nobody was seriously hurt.

produced_by: Automatic Emergency Braking active on a Tesla Model X whose cameras and radar register an obstacle entering its path
A hazard that arrives in front of the car, here a tree falling across the carriageway, rather than onto the roof from above
A stop short of the point where the trunk lands, leaving the bonnet rather than the cabin to take the impact
must_hold: The system has time to detect and brake, which Sanderson put at about a second

Occupants are belted. The Whitelock passengers were sore from the seatbelts
